items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was there any other trumpet player you liked in addition to Louie, Emmanuel, and Lee Collins?

ctx.x: Oh yes. Well, that was practically the trend around there. If I listened to the guys, if you listened to the guys, you wouldn't even want to listen. Yeah, that's right. If you listened to the older guys, the majority of the old guys, you wouldn't hardly want to listen even. No kidding. Because if it don't be familiar, I don't guess I'd ever want to listen. Not in that era, because they were music conscious, which nowadays the guys, the youngsters, they have a better advantage of that. They don't do that anymore.…
Was there any other trumpet player you liked in addition to Louie, Emmanuel, and Lee Collins? Did you hear Chris Kelly much?

Oh, Chris Kelly, yes. Well, I just forgot the name of Bill. In those days I practically, I knew every guy, I knew every guy in those days that was playing and everything. And Bunk, oh, Bunk, you know, Bunk here, stop and he'd start over and he'd stop and he'd start over. But I knew Bunk and everything. I met him lots of time. I knew Iberia when I was working with Paul. Oh, you'd known him over there? Yes, I used to go with Isaiah Morgan, Ike Morgan, Sam Morgan's brother. Well, I played with him a lot, you know.…
